script.base: Spread and total are not in the pack, so the book's expected leader and scoring environment are unknown and this script is form-only. Both quarterbacks have been inefficient (IND EPA/dropback -0.19 vs blitz and -0.21 with no blitz; PIT -0.39 vs blitz and -0.06 with no blitz), while the run games are the stable piece: Jonathan Taylor 67 carries for 255 yards and Jaylen Warren 45 carries for 263 over weeks 2-4. Base case is a competitive, run-tilted game in which Warren keeps about a 15-carry role into IND's 4.97 YPC run defense and Pittsburgh still throws, because IND blitzes only 20%, enough for DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson to hold recent target shares.
script.flip1: If Indianapolis blitzes above its 20% rate, Aaron Rodgers' EPA/dropback falls to -0.39 (n=46) and Pittsburgh trails, so Warren's carries shrink and targets funnel to Metcalf (23 targets, 290 air yards) and Wilson (18 targets, 242 air yards).
script.flip2: If Pittsburgh gets ahead and clocks it with Warren (5.84 YPC over the last 3), IND pass volume stalls: Josh Downs (24 targets, 165 yards) and Tyler Warren (22 targets, 117 yards, only 36 air yards) become the short-area options while Pittsburgh explosives undershoot.

Roman Wilson's 242 air yards overlap IND's leaky left and middle, but he is not the primary: DK Metcalf has 23 targets and 290 air yards into the same zones.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because Warren's 5.84 YPC was a three-game heater: IND stacked the box, Kenneth Gainwell is not in this pack but Dowdle (7 carries) and Homer (5) vultured touches, and the negative-air checkdowns stayed under 25 yards so scrimmage finished under 99. Wilson's 54-yard average was explosive-dependent against a defense with only 13 passes of 20+ on 144 attempts, Metcalf's 290 air yards took the downfield shots, and a Pittsburgh lead turned the fourth quarter into Warren clock-kills so Wilson never saw a fourth target.
slip_story: One story: Pittsburgh's offense functions because IND allows 4.97 YPC and blitzes only 20%, Rodgers' less-bad split. Anchor is Warren rushrecyds over 99. Companion is Wilson recyds over 41, tagged script-dependent because it needs Pittsburgh to keep throwing and dies in the clock-kill flip. Do not pair with a Pittsburgh unders stack, a Warren rush under, or a Metcalf/Wilson under. Taylor rush over 84.5 is a separate IND clock-kill idea and is off this slip because 85.0 equals the 84.5 line.
